newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk MPs abandon Islamists, Yilmaz near majority.
newsitem.headline: Turk MPs abandon Islamists, Yilmaz near majority.

text.p: Four Turkish MPs quit a pro-Islamist alliance on Friday, taking secularist Mesut Yilmaz close to the majority he needs to win a confidence vote in his coalition government.
Three conservative True Path Party deputies and an Islamist from the Welfare Party resigned in one-paragraph letters submitted to the parliamentary speaker's office.
The resignations reduced the Islamists and their allies to 275 MPs on paper, compared with 272 deputies who are likely to back Yilmaz at the vote, expected within two weeks.
A spokesman for Yilmaz's Motherland Party predicted the anti-Islamists would easily win parliamentary backing for their left-right coalition.
"This government is not going to win by just a hair's breadth, it will comfortably carry the confidence vote," senior Motherland member Murat Basesgioglu told a news conference.
Istanbul shares jumped nearly five percent by late morning on rising hopes that Yilmaz can form a coalition to prevent an Islamist return to power.
Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan resigned a week ago under pressure from the military but he plans to get back into office in a revamped coalition led by conservative partner Tansu Ciller.
Secularist politicians were to begin drawing up the Yilmaz government programme and working out the distribution of ministries on Friday.
They hope to present President Suleyman Demirel with a cabinet list next Monday or Tuesday and take over the reins of government before the confidence vote.
